meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong regulatory and commercial law influence)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Article 12 of Law 2010 of 2019; Decree 1299 of 2021; DIAN Resolution 000164 of 2022; Law 1121 of 2007; Law 526 of 1999; UIAF Circular DCIP 002 of 2023

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs (if issued in Colombia)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Public Deed of Incorporation or Private Articles of Incorporation (Acta de Constitución)
Legalized Power of Attorney executed by each shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if signatory country party to HCCH 1961) or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and internal filing; apostille not required for domestic filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC SDN, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UIAF's National Lists, and domestic criminal asset forfeiture screening; enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons, remote onboarding, and cross-border payroll flows; ongoing transaction monitoring under Law 1121 of 2007 and UIAF Circular DCIP 002 of 2023.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) via Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be in Spanish or in a Latin-script transliteration; no abbreviation or phonetic equivalent that misleads as to legal form; must include the suffix 'S.A.S.'; name may not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered trademark or entity name in the RUES database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a recurso de reposición directly with the responsible Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of notice; if the rejection is maintained, the applicant may file recurso de apelación before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio. All appeal filings must be made through the same RUES portal or writing to the chamber, attaching the initial clearance application and rejection resolution.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible only if the registered office provides a physical address in Colombia where demand letters and court notices may be served; a P.O. Box alone is not accepted. For S.A.S. companies operating as payroll SaaS, a virtual office with a physical rented desk or shared space is acceptable, provided that the business maintains its principal books and records accessible for inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation fee at Cámara de Comercio (RUES)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Superintendencia de Sociedades

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of articles of incorporation and shareholders' minutes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notary tariff, based on capital and number of instruments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registry registration fee for S.A.S. (including company registration and NIT/RUT provisional)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on asset value / fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO initial filing and reporting (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark / legal compliance fee; DIAN registration is zero-fee but legal professional preparation applied

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Colombia) or designated consular authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prescribed government fee for apostille per document + translation fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of articles of incorporation and power of attorney (Spanish/English)
Legal drafting and pre-incorporation due diligence (fixed fee)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Artículos 5, 17 y 22; Código de Comercio, Artículos 110 y 354; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Libro 2, Parte 2, Título 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social principal (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), Registro Único Empresarial.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private instrument) filed for registration in the Mercantile Registry; public deed required only if real property is contributed as capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital. Share capital is freely subscribed in the articles; payment terms may be deferred up to two years unless in-kind contributions (which require valuation). No escrow account mandated by law, but bank accounts should receive corporate funds before commencing tax obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF SHAREHOLDERS OF [SAS NAME] — WHEREAS the company was incorporated by private instrument and legally registered; and WHEREAS the initial subscribed capital has been duly allocated among shareholders. NOW IT IS RESOLVED: (1) Ratify the incorporation instrument and approve the subscribed shares in their entirety. (2) Designate the registered office at [address], Bogotá, Colombia, and authorize the execution of lease or use agreements. (3) Appoint the following officers: [President/Representante Legal] and [Secretario], with the powers provided in the bylaws. (4) Instruct the President to open a corporate bank account and pay all registration and public registry fees. (5) Approve the immediate commencement of lawful business operations. This Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Drafting of Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (online portal: www.ccb.org.co / RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application to reserve the proposed company name; use the online merchant registry (RUES) to verify the name is not identical to a registered entity. Draft the private instrument incorporating the SAS, including name, domicile, corporate purpose (software development and payroll automation services), share classes, capital structure, and governance rules. Ensure all shareholder signatures are authenticated (notarized if required).
required_dossiers: Description of corporate purpose and capital allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected, file an appeal with the Chamber of Commerce or select an alternative name and resubmit immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registry Filing and Incorporation Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the fully executed private instrument and required attachments to the Cámara de Comercio window or upload through the RUES online portal. Pay the registration fee and stamp tax. Upon approval, the Chamber issues the Certificate of Business Existence (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal). This certificate authorizes the SAS to operate.
required_dossiers: Completed single business registration form (Formulario RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises deficiencies (e.g., clarifications on corporate purpose), correct the instrument by a private amendment signed by all shareholders and resubmit within the granted term; request expedited re-review for time-sensitive filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Corporate Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) and commercial banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with DIAN to obtain the RUT (Registro Único Tributario). Select the applicable fiscal regime (ordinary income and complementary tax, ICMS if applicable). Open a corporate bank account by presenting the RUT, the Certificate of Existence, the bylaws, and board resolution; ensure the legal representative's identification and a compliance officer are registered for AML/KYC.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN queries the RUT application (e.g., mismatch of address or activity), submit a corrective online form (energía virtual) and provide supplementary documentation; escalate to DIAN's attention window if the query remains unresolved beyond 3 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Permit and Physical Office Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local mayor's office (Alcaldía) and municipal planning department (Curaduría Urbana)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business license (Registro de Industria y Comercio) and the urban land-use certificate (Certificado de Uso del Suelo) for the office premises. Confirm the location permits commercial software development and administrative office activities. Display the issued certificate at the registered office. For payroll SaaS, no industry-specific technical license is required under Colombian law.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Lease agreement or ownership deed for the office
Identification and tax ID (NIT) of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the intended address lacks a compatible land-use designation, submit a revised application for a conditional use permit (Aprovechamiento en Subsidio) or relocate to a permitted office zone; appeal denied certificates before the municipal planning authority or via extraordinary writ (acción de tutela) if rights violate due process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specific industrial licensing body for software development; general municipal authority is the Alcaldía through its Industry and Commerce Office (Registro de Industria y Comercio).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Industria y Comercio (municipal business registration) and Certificado de Uso del Suelo.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) or municipal environmental authority (Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — software development and data processing services are not in the list of projects requiring environmental impact assessment under Decree 1076 of 2015, Artículo 2.2.2.3.2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for production; office waste must comply with common commercial waste disposal norms (waste segregation and recycling under Resolución 2184 de 2019). If servers are operated, comply with voltage and thermal management best practices, and dispose of e-waste through licensed recyclers under Colombian electronic waste regulations (Resolución 1512 de 2010).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Bomberos) issued by the local fire department, verifying the office has functional extinguishers, emergency routes, and adequate occupancy load. Occupancy must comply with structural and electrical safety inspections as reflected in the SIC (Sistema de Inspección y Vigilancia) workplace clearance; if the office has more than 50 workers, a formal occupational health and safety program (SG-SST) is mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — Colombia's national tax, customs and foreign-exchange control authority; digital services portal: https://www.dian.gov.co (Sede Electrónica / Sistema de Facturación Electrónica).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Obtain the provisional NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) electronically through DIAN's PRE-RUT/VUE channel during SAS incorporation, before registration with the Cámara de Comercio. STEP 2: After Cámara de Comercio registration, finalize the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) with the definitive NIT, corporate data, ISIC/CIU code 6201, VAT responsibility status (19% IVA 'Régimen Común'), and withholding-agent duties. STEP 3: Non-resident shareholders or foreign investors without a Colombian branch must register a tax-resident fiscal representative on the RUT per the statutory representation rules of the Colombian Tax Code; if the foreign investor operates through a local office or agency, register the sucursal or establecimiento permanente as a separate taxpayer. STEP 4: Obtain the mandatory digital signature/certificate from a DIAN-authorized certification provider and enable the electronic-invoicing profile (FEV/CUFE) plus the payroll e-invoicing profile (Nómina Electrónica). STEP 5: Register the service-export reporting obligation (Form 340 services-export declaration) and open the foreign-exchange channeling procedures with the Banco de la República.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Colombian domestic law. Available statutory elections include: (i) Colombian Holding Company (CHC) regime per Law 1943 de 2018 / Law 2010 de 2019 for qualifying holding entities, with exemption treatment for foreign dividends and capital gains; (ii) Régimen Simple de Tributación (RST) integrated tax regime for eligible SMEs with annual gross income not exceeding 100,000 UVT; (iii) Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) with DIAN for transfer-pricing certainty; (iv) optional presumptive cost/profit percentage regimes for specified sectors; and (v) conclusive settlement mechanisms for challenged tax positions, at DIAN's discretion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia, acting with the Junta Directiva as the ultimate monetary and exchange authority; the foreign-exchange regulatory framework is principally codified in Resolución Externa No. 1 of 2018 and Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83. The Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) supervises all Authorized Intermediaries of the Exchange Market (intermediarios del mercado cambiario, or IMCs), and the Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF) administers the anti-money-laundering reporting regime governing banking onboarding and cross-border transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) operates under a managed-floating exchange-rate regime. Current-account transactions — trade in software services, royalties, lease payments, interest on external debt, and occasional transfers such as profit remittances and family remittances — are fully convertible absent prior authorization, but every such payment must be 'canalized' (channeled) through an Authorized Intermediary of the Exchange Market (IMC) by filing a Declaración de Cambio (foreign-exchange declaration). Capital-account inflows, including non-resident direct equity investment in the Colombian SAS, are freely permitted but must be registered with Banco de la República through Form 3 (Registro de Inversiones Internacionales); without such registration, the non-resident investor loses the legal right to remit dividends through the regulated exchange market and to repatriate capital proceeds. The principal profit-remittance hurdles are: (i) proof of a valid foreign-investment registration, (ii) corporate approval of the dividend distribution by the shareholders' meeting, (iii) certification by the registered public accountant (contador público) that the profits are distributable and have borne the applicable corporate income tax, (iv) payment of the 7.5% dividend withholding tax applicable to non-residents for profits declared from earnings subject to tax at the standard corporate rate, and (v) verification that the underlying dividend payment is declared to the IMC under the correct exchange-market concept code and accompanied by the dividend act, financial statements, and tax-cleared profit confirmation. There are no exchange-licensing restrictions on the amount of profit that may be repatriated once the aforementioned documentary obligations are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exports of services (including the Payroll-SaaS software platform), the exporter must 'reintegrate' the foreign-currency proceeds into Colombia through an IMC within six (6) months counted from the date of issuance of the export invoice or, per prevailing Banco de la República interpretation, from the date of the respective income (devengo); goods exports are reintegrated within six (6) months from the shipment (embarque) date. The mandatory channeling obligation is effectively 100% of the export proceeds: the exporter must either sell the foreign currency to an IMC or deposit it in a Banco de la República-authorized foreign-currency account (cuenta de compensación) previously registered with the Exchange Market, and the corresponding declaración de cambio must be filed with the IMC. There is no fixed percentage split between forced conversion and retention because the full amount of proceeds must be canalized; retention in foreign currency is possible only through a registered compensation account or, during a temporary statutory window, through a 'cuenta de destinación específica' at the IMC. Failure to reintegrate within the six-month term triggers monetary fines imposed by Banco de la República and may cause Directorate of Taxes (DIAN) enforcement for customs/metrics mismatches.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for Registered Foreign Investment (Cuenta de Inversión Internacional) plus Operational COP/USD payroll account
Capital Escrow Account for Registered Foreign Investment plus Operational COP payroll account with ACH and corporate-card rails
Operational COP account with integrated foreign-investment registration module; Capital Escrow Account available for cross-border wires
Operational COP account and USD-denominated IMC account for FX channeling of software export proceeds
Current-account and payroll clearing account; institutional treasury line for COP/USD forwards

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium and legally constrained. Colombia does not recognise foreign electronic-money-institution (EMI) licences as authorisation to take deposits or to operate ACH direct-debit payroll rails in COP; regulated electronic-payment activity is limited to Colombian SFC-licensed SEDPEs (Sociedades Especializadas en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos). Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Mercury) and similar Banking-as-a-Service aggregators can lawfully provide supplementary SWIFT corridors for low-value cross-border collections or disbursements, but they cannot be the primary treasury bank because (i) they are not IMCs, (ii) they cannot receive the required Form 3 capital-investment declaration, (iii) they cannot originate local ACH-COL payroll debits, and (iv) force of law mandates FX channeling through regulated IMCs. Therefore, the recommended treasury configuration is a domestic Tier-1 IMC bank as the authorised account owner and a remote EMI as a non-essential overflow corridor only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned SAS opening a bank account in Colombia, physical presence of the legal representative is the standard rule for Tier-1 commercial banks: at least one in-branch appearance at final onboarding is required, together with a compliance interview with the SFC-mandated official responsible for SARLAFT (Sistema de Administración del Riesgo de Lavado de Activos y Financiación del Terrorismo). Remote-only openings are exceptionally granted by some banks (e.g., Bancolombia's digital onboarding channel for SAS entities) but generally require: a notarised business record and apostilled certificate of existence; a certified power of attorney (poder especial) in favor of a Colombian-resident attorney-in-fact for signature authority; a compliance video-call to verify the ultimate beneficial owner; and submission of all corporate documents in Spanish or with certified Spanish translation. For a 100% foreign-controlled payroll-SaaS entity, the prudential posture of major banks will effectively mandate an in-country legal representative or a Colombian-resident signatory, because the bank's risk department needs an accountable physical contact for SARLAFT duties and source-of-funds queries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque offshore beneficial-ownership chain holding a material interest in the SAS (shareholders registered in jurisdictions not separated from ultimate individuals)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete registered ownership chain from each individual ultimate beneficial owner to the SAS; apostilled certificates of incorporation for each upstream corporate shareholder; certified Spanish translations of registry extracts; organisational chart signed by the SAS legal representative; sworn statement of ownership and source of wealth; copy of the SAS by-laws showing share-transfer restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or key director appearing on PEP lists or sanctions/negative-news databases (World-Check, LexisNexis, OFAC)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP declaration with explanation of the public-office relationship; evidence of lawful income (prior-year tax filings, audited financial statements, employment contracts); resignation or nomination certificate if the PEP role was terminated; independent professional references from attorneys/accountants; if the PEP status remains, the file must include an SFC-compliant enhanced due-diligence packet with documented source-of-funds and source-of-wealth analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Prior treasury flows involving cryptocurrencies or fund receipts from virtual-asset service providers used to capitalise the SAS
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original exchange off-ramp statements proving conversion of crypto to fiat; screenshot-level ledger of the originating crypto wallet; signed source-of-funds affidavit by each capital contributor; underlying commercial agreements for software services that generated the legitimate earnings; payroll-customer contracts and invoices substantiating the business purpose of the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder resident in a high-risk/high-tax-transparency-concern jurisdiction, or existence of shell-company indicators with no economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD business-purpose statement; audited financial statements of the shareholder; proof of substantive offices/employees (lease, utility invoices, social-security records); group structure chart evidencing the strategic reason for the Colombian SAS (nearshore software delivery); certification from a reputable foreign regulator or a local counsel opinion on the shareholder's legitimate activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, volatile volume of cross-border Payroll-SaaS remittances with no clear nexus to local employees or local substance in Colombia
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed payroll services agreements with Colombian end-clients and international clients; payroll run documentation showing ISIC-6201 software processing, employee count, and COP payment schedule; RUT showing taxable operation in Colombia; intragroup service/output contracts; revenue invoices matched to SWIFT messages; appointment of a Colombian compliance officer and adoption of a SARLAFT manual.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must inject equity exclusively via international SWIFT wire (MT103 for direct transfers, MT202 cover for interbank reimbursement) from their own banking institution to the IMC-designated 'Cuenta de Capital' (capital escrow/registration account) of the Colombian SAS, with the wire reference carrying the SAS's RUT and the shareholder's name. The eligible foreign-investment registration file (Form 3 - Registro de Inversiones Internacionales) must be presented simultaneously to the IMC through the foreign-exchange declaration module; the capital must be channeled under the Banco de la República canalization concept code corresponding to direct international investment by non-resident shareholders (as enumerated in the DCIN-83 Circular's exchange-concept annex). Verification evidence must include: (i) the issuer's bank wire confirmation with purpose text 'Aporte de capital a sociedad SAS - Inversión Directa Internacional', (ii) the corporate capital-contribution agreement (acuerdo de suscripción de acciones) executed before a notary, (iii) the minutes of the extraordinary shareholders' meeting approving the capital increase, (iv) the RUT and certificate of existence of the SAS, (v) the updated foreign-investment registration certificate issued by the IMC, and (vi) for any subsequent distributions, the corresponding Form 3 updates and annual registry filings. There is no prior Central Bank authorisation requirement on the quantum of capital, but the investment must be registered to preserve future dividend repatriation and capital-exit rights.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of trade and non-trade liabilities, the primary outbound rail is the domestic SWIFT network via the IMC: MT103 messages for vendor/subcontractor payments, software-license fees, and shareholder dividend remittances; MT202 for nostro/IMC interbank cover in USD or EUR. For high-value procurement contracts (e.g., unused infrastructure licenses, equipment, mergers or acquisition targets abroad), Colombian banks operate commercial letters of credit (documentary L/C) under UCP 600, with the SAS as applicant and confirmation through the beneficiary's overseas bank. For payroll and low-value peso payments inside Colombia, the exclusive clearing rail is the ACH-COL system (ACH Colombia S.A.) which settles through the Banco de la República's CENIT real-time gross-settlement platform; direct debits are pre-notified via payroll files using the employee's account number, bank routing code, and the 'pago de nómina' payment instruction. All FX-denominated outflows must be canalized under the appropriate current-account concept (import of services, royalty payment, dividend distribution) and the corresponding Declaración de Cambio must be filed at the IMC within the statutory deadline, with documentary backup (invoice, contract, tax withholding proof) preserved for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/COP deliverable outright forwards (forwards) executed exclusively with an Authorized Intermediary of the Exchange Market (IMC) on the basis of a real, documented underlying current-account or capital-account exposure (SAS software cross-border receivables, dividend flows, capital remittances).

USD/COP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted to be traded onshore through IMCs for hedging the same Colombian peso-denominated cash-flow exposure, typically liquid for tenors of up to 12 months; the company must demonstrate absence of speculation and must settle any net payment through the regulated exchange market.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (COP-USD) permissible for the SAS to align external-debt cash flows and capital repatriation timing, provided they are booked with an IMC or a Bancolombia/Banco de Bogotá swap desk and comply with SFC prudential regulatory requirements (Position and counterparty exposure).

Vanilla foreign-currency options (USD/COP put and call) bought from an IMC for tail-risk protection of the payroll and licensing cost base, with premium payable in COP; options may not be sold naked by a non-financial SAS onshore.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the commercial registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (local Chamber of Commerce) via the Single Business Registry (RUES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March; the deadline is not renewable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers interest charges and a surcharge of 3% per month on the renewal fee; continued non-renewal may result in fines up to 18 current statutory monthly minimum wages, loss of good-standing certification, and administrative cancellation of the mercantile registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statement deposit and filing of approved results (Estados Financieros de Propósito General)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (through RUES) after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies: the ordinary shareholders' meeting must be held by 31 March and the financial statements must be deposited with the Chamber by 30 April (within one month after approval).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit may result in fines of up to 1% of the book value of assets or 10 SMMLV, whichever is greater; the company also loses the ability to obtain a good-standing certificate and to carry out certain corporate acts until the filing is completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and complementary return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually for the prior tax year; the exact due date is set by DIAN Resolution based on the employer's NIT, with a general calendar window between mid-April and late May for calendar-year entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax plus monthly default interest; if DYIAN assess the return after a formal warning, the penalty is 10% of tax due; persistent non-filing may lead to bank-account embargo, asset seizure, and criminal tax-evasion charges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Unified annual information return for third-party transactions (Información Exógena)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, according to the DIAN Resolution calendar, generally from 15 July through 31 August depending on NIT suffix; covers payroll, shareholder and supplier information of the prior fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or material omissions can generate fines up to 20,000 UVT, loss of deductibility for unreported expenses and payments, and a full DIAN review of payroll and vendor records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of ultimate beneficial owners (Reporte de Beneficiarios Finales / RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the period selected by DIAN for the applicable tax year, generally in the second quarter; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 15 calendar days after being recorded in the shareholder register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting, under-reporting or false UBO information may result in fines up to 20,000 UVT, anti-money-laundering suspension measures, and blocked dividend distributions or corporate resolutions until compliance is restored.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified public accountant acting as Revisor Fiscal is mandatory if, at the prior fiscal year-end, the entity has total assets or gross income exceeding 5,000 current statutory minimum monthly salaries (SMMLV), or if the entity has more than 15 employees; the thresholds are measured in Colombian pesos under Colombian GAAP.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP, comprising IFRS as incorporated by Decree 2496 of 2015 for Grupo 1 and Grupo 2 taxpayers and IFRS for SMEs for eligible SME-SASs; statutory financial statements must be expressed in Colombian pesos and prepared in Spanish.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Colombian SAS must maintain a current shareholder register identifying each accepted shareholder under civil-law control. Any transfer of shares modifies beneficial ownership and must be recorded in the shareholder register, approved in the minute book, and reflected in the DIAN annual RUBF report. An annual confirmation is filed with DIAN every calendar year, even if no transfer occurred, and must be certified by the legal representative resident in Colombia.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors and Attendance (Libro de Asistencia y Actas de Juntas Directivas)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,200 per year for a registered office address and corporate administration (Cámara/Comercio representation) in Bogotá or Medellín
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - 5,000 per year for an independent certified accountant (Revisor Fiscal or independent auditor) where the entity meets the audit thresholds or otherwise chooses voluntary audit support
